title: Auth Control Plane refresh exchange response (v1 wire format)
description: A successful refresh: a new access token in today's HS256 ops format (kept until Wave 3) and the ROTATED opaque refresh credential. Rotation is single use with a 30 s concurrent-refresh grace (the grace answer returns the same successor). The old user object is not part of this contract; clients read session.v1.

schema_version.description: Contract identifier. A reader MUST reject an unrecognised value (G-26: unknown denies); additive evolution stays in v1 (TRD section 21).

access_token.description: Compact JWS whose protected header is EXACTLY the HS256 header the ops signer emits ({"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}, internal/auth/edgetoken/signer.go headerSegment). Pinning the header segment refuses RS256, ES256 and alg=none in every reader; the asymmetric access token arrives in Wave 3 as a new surface version. Lifetime is unchanged from go-api (60 minutes).

expires_in.description: Access token lifetime in seconds: exactly 3600 (60 minutes), go-api's accessExpiresIn, until the asymmetric issuer of Wave 3 changes it. Integer token only; 3600.0 passes the schema (const compares numbers) and both clients refuse it.

refresh_credential.description: Opaque refresh credential: URL-safe base64 characters only, 43-256 long. A dot is not in the alphabet, so a refresh JWT cannot be presented here. A SECRET: it exists on the wire only in the refresh request and the refresh response, never in session.v1 or auth-outcome.v1, never in a log, metric label or audit row.

refresh_expires_in.description: Rotated refresh credential lifetime in seconds; the 7 day ceiling is today's RefreshLifetime.

session_id.description: Opaque server-minted session identifier. An identifier, never a secret, and never copied from caller input.
